 Follow Why Tom Cruise 'punched' Jack Nicholson on set: The truth behind the surprising moment
 Jovita Trujillo Fri, October 23, 2026 at 11:20 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Why Tom Cruise 'punched' Jack Nicholson on set: The truth behind the surprising moment (Tomohiro Ohsumi) One of the most intense scenes in Tom Cruise's career apparently had a much lighter atmosphere behind the cameras. More than three decades after the release of 'A Few Good Men,' actor Kevin Pollak is revisiting a hilarious moment involving Cruise and Jack Nicholson that ended with an unexpected punch.
 Tom Cruise and Jack Nicholson shared one of Hollywood's most memorable courtroom confrontations in the 1992 film A Few Good Men. (@ Mondadori Portfolio)
 During a recent appearance on Steve Kmetko's 'Still Here Hollywood' podcast, Pollak, who starred alongside the two Hollywood legends in the 1992 legal drama, recalled how Nicholson deliberately tried to distract Cruise while filming their famous courtroom confrontation.
 The scene, which features Cruise's Lieutenant Daniel Kaffee demanding the truth from Nicholson's Colonel Nathan Jessup, has become one of the most recognizable moments in movie history. But according to Pollak, Nicholson had a mischievous way of keeping his co-star on his toes.
 What really happened between Tom Cruise and Jack Nicholson?
 Pollak explained that Nicholson was positioned close to the camera during a particularly intense take, giving Cruise a rather unusual sight as he delivered his lines.
 Jack Nicholson at the premiere of A Few Good Men in 1992. (@ Ron Galella)
 "Jack is doing this, making the most ridiculous clown face you've ever seen," Pollak recalled, demonstrating the actor's exaggerated expression during the podcast. Despite Nicholson's attempts to make him laugh, Cruise remained focused and completed the scene without breaking character.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "And Tom stayed in the pocket and finished the scene and then punched Jack Nicholson in the shoulder," Pollak said, adding that both actors burst into laughter afterward.
 Nicole Kidman and Tom Cruise attend the premiere of A Few Good Men in Westwood, California, on December 9, 1992. (@ Ron Galella, Ltd.)
 The playful exchange offers a surprising glimpse into the dynamic between the two stars, whose heated on-screen confrontation became a defining moment of the Oscar-nominated film.
 Tom Cruise previously revealed what it was like working with Jack Nicholson
 Interestingly, Cruise has also spoken about his unforgettable experience filming the courtroom sequence with Nicholson.
 Jack Nicholson as Colonel Nathan Jessup in the 1992 courtroom drama A Few Good Men. (@ Getty Images)
 During a 2025 conversation with the British Film Institute, the 'Mission: Impossible' star recalled how word spread around Hollywood that the two actors were preparing to shoot their dramatic confrontation.
 Advertisement Advertisement "I couldn't wait to do that scene with him," Cruise said, explaining that people from across the industry gathered at Culver Studios to watch them perform.
 Tom Cruise was determined to stay in character despite Jack Nicholson's hilarious attempts to distract him during filming. (@ Pool ARNAL/GARCIA/PICOT)
 The actor described Nicholson as an exceptionally generous scene partner who remained engaged even when the camera wasn't focused on him. "Jack is very much an actor's actor, and was there off-camera the whole time, very giving and gracious," Cruise recalled.
 His comments paint a picture of mutual admiration between the two performers, making Pollak's latest anecdote even more entertaining.
 The lasting legacy of 'A Few Good Men'
 Directed by Rob Reiner and written by Aaron Sorkin, 'A Few Good Men' follows a military lawyer defending two Marines accused of killing a fellow serviceman.
 Advertisement Advertisement The film also stars Demi Moore, Kevin Bacon and Kiefer Sutherland and earned four Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture and Best Supporting Actor for Nicholson.
 Tom Cruise listening to Director Rob Reiner in between scenes from the film 'A Few Good Men', 1992. (@ Archive Photos)
 Pollak previously reflected on the film's surprisingly relaxed working environment, recalling a lesson he learned from Reiner about the importance of enjoying the creative process, even while making an intense courtroom drama.
 Decades later, the story of Nicholson's playful antics and Cruise's unexpected response reveals a side of their legendary collaboration that audiences never saw on screen.
